newsitem.title: CANADA: MPE to put more custom orders in mid-size elevator.
newsitem.headline: MPE to put more custom orders in mid-size elevator.

text.p: Manitoba Pool Elevators plans to handle more custom grain orders through its mid-sized facilities in 1997/98 (Aug/July), MPE's president said.

"It's extremely difficult to carry out an identity-preserved program (end-user custom order) in high-through put elevators because they've got large bins, so, for some smaller elevators there is a role to play," MPE president Charlie Swanson told Reuters in an interview.
MPE, a farmer-owned agricultural cooperative, is in its third year handling custom orders for specific types of wheat to British baker Warburtons.
Millers, crushers and other end users were expected to seek more custom orders in the future to remain competitive, grain industry leaders said.
MPE plans to ship entire train loads of one commodity to U.S. end-users in 1997/98 (Aug/July) by using mid-sized 7,500 tonne elevators instead of 12,000-tonne high through put ones.
"We've shipped 25-car (trains) of oats, flax and milling wheat into the U.S. market in the last crop year and we expect to continue to do that," Swanson said.
Mid-sized elevators used for dedicated train runs should turn inventory over eight to 10 times a year, he added.
MPE's elevator stock turnover rate in 1996/97 rose to an average seven times a year versus 5.5 in 1995/96, he said.
"We moved a bigger crop but our licensed capacity hasn't changed that much in the last few years," Swanson said.

While the cooperative handled 3.3 million tonnes of product in 1996/97 compared to 2.6 million tonnes in 1995/96, it's primary elevator space was unchanged at 500,000 tonnes, or 49 percent of Manitoba's total capacity, he said.
